root_idea.summary: The root centers on abasement: being reduced to a low, contemptible, or submissive state.
root_idea.development: The intransitive Form I denotes being or becoming abject, while Form IV expresses causing another to become abject. The Quranic active participle denotes those in the resulting state. The storage-related forms ادّخر and مُدَّخِرٌ are treated as belonging to a different lexical branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form corresponding to the Quranic plural occurrences.

senses.definition: Abject, humbled, or brought low; in a state of humiliation and submissive lowliness.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle naming one who is or has become abject. The supplied Quranic contexts range from humble submission to humiliating abasement; these are contextual expressions of the same lexical state, not separate senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render another abject, mean, contemptible, or despicable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative and transitive: to cause someone to enter a state of abasement.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form I state of being or becoming abject is represented by the Quranic active-participle sense.
The causative Form IV meaning is represented as a broader Classical meaning.

cautions: The forms ادّخر and مُدَّخِرٌ are explicitly referred to the ذخر branch associated with storing or saving, not the Quranic دخر branch of abasement.
